stem: A child has hypoplastic clavicles, supernumerary teeth and delayed eruption of the permanent teeth; which condition best fits this pattern?
explanation: Cleidocraniodysplasia is the correct diagnosis because the combination of hypoplastic clavicles, supernumerary teeth and delayed eruption of permanent teeth is characteristic of this condition.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because holoprosencephaly is associated with midline craniofacial anomalies such as a single central incisor, not hypoplastic clavicles and extra teeth.
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because osteogenesis imperfecta is classically associated with dentinogenesis imperfecta and blue sclera, not this clavicle and dental pattern.
optionExplanations.C: Correct because cleidocraniodysplasia classically causes hypoplastic clavicles, supernumerary teeth and delayed eruption of the permanent dentition.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because a normal maxillary frenum is a benign anatomical finding and does not explain this syndromic presentation.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because ectodermal dysplasia can affect teeth and other ectodermal structures, but this specific pattern of clavicular hypoplasia and delayed eruption is more typical of cleidocraniodysplasia.
